title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide introduces contrastive learning as an objective that maximizes the similarity of positive pairs while minimizing the similarity of negative pairs. It accompanies this with a schematic of a two-branch architecture in which a query image and a key image are each passed through an encoder, and a loss is computed on the resulting representations. Annotations note that both encoders are updated and that they share weights.

visuals.description: Two-branch pipeline: a query image and a key image each feed into an Encoder block; outputs meet at a loss node. Labels indicate both encoders are updated and weights are shared between them.
visuals.assertion: Contrastive training uses a siamese, weight-shared two-encoder setup where query and key embeddings are compared through a contrastive loss and both branches receive gradient updates.
